sanitized_snapshot.failure_description:
[body] On Windows the `if NO_MAN_PAGES or os.system == 'nt':` branch is dead code. The function does not short-circuit; instead it falls through to `subprocess.run(['man', '1', program])`. On a typical Windows install `man` is absent, so `FileNotFoundError` is raised and swallowed by the `except Exception: return False`, yielding the same observable result — but only by accident. If a `man` executable happens to be on `PATH` (e.g. Git Bash / WSL), HTTPie will attempt to render man pages on Windows, contrary to the intent of the guard. Also, relying on a swallowed exception for control flow is fragile.
[body] ## Affected version
sanitized_snapshot.title: Bug: Windows guard in is_available() compares os.system (a function) to 'nt' — always False

[body] Currently, the execution of this example raises: `ValidationError: {'sentinel': ['Field may not be null.']}`.
[body] However, in Python, enum members can have `None` as values. From that perspective, it might be expected that `None` would be treated as part of the field's value domain when using `by_value=True`. According to the documentation, if this parameter is set to `True`, it delegates deserialization to `fields.Raw`, which has its own mechanism to deal with None values before the enum value resolution occurs.
[body] This observation was raised by an automated testing tool currently being developed by our research team. Before submitting this issue, we tested the example in the last development version of marshmallow and reviewed the related documentation. 
[comment] Should explicitly setting `allow_none` to `False` still produce the error? Setting a `by_value` field errors when an otherwise valid value doesn't match the type.
[comment:code] # marshmallow.exceptions.ValidationError: {'sentinel': ['Not a valid string.']}
[comment] i think explicitly setting `allow_none=False` should be allowed and produce an error when `None` is loaded.

sanitized_snapshot.failure_description:
[body] When pluggy tracing is enabled (e.g. pytest's `--debug` flag), hook arguments or return values containing surrogate escape characters (like `\ud800`) cause a `UnicodeEncodeError` crash. This is because `_format_message` in `_tracing.py` uses `str()` to format values, and the resulting string with literal surrogates cannot be written to most output targets.
[body] Reported originally as pytest-dev/pytest#13750.
[body:code]   finish pytest_runtest_call --> '\ud800' [hook]
[body] Rather than the over-quoted version that blanket `repr()` in `_format_message` would produce:
[body:code]   'finish' 'pytest_runtest_call' '-->' "'\\ ud800'" [hook]
[body] - pytest-dev/pytest#13750
sanitized_snapshot.title: Tracing crashes with UnicodeEncodeError on surrogate escapes in hook arguments/results

sanitized_snapshot.failure_description:
[body] `ade install . -e` builds the local collection by copying paths from `git ls-files`. If the working tree has deleted or moved tracked files without updating the index (e.g. after `ansible-creator migrate molecule` relocates `tests/integration/targets/` → `extensions/molecule/`), ADE raises an **uncaught** `FileNotFoundError` instead of a clear user-facing error.
[body] It should not dump a traceback for this case — detect missing paths and fail with a helpful message (list missing files / suggest staging or restoring them).
[body]    - e.g. migrate integration targets so `tests/integration/targets/...` is gone on disk but still listed by `git ls-files`
[body] ### Actual behavior
[body:code] Traceback (most recent call last):
[body:code] FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../tests/integration/targets/utils_cli_parse/files/nxos_show_interface.txt'
[body] ### Expected behavior
[body] - No raw traceback for missing tracked files.
[body] - Clear error naming the missing path(s) and that ADE copies from `git ls-files` (index), so unstaged deletes/moves will break install until staged/committed or restored.
[body] `_copy_repo_files` in `subcommands/installer.py` iterates `git ls-files` and calls `shutil.copy2`. `FileNotFoundError` is not handled (existing `except shutil.Error` does not catch it). New untracked paths (the move destination) are also omitted from the copy set until staged.

[body] `MultiChannelProcessGroup._broadcast` catches Gloo broadcast failures and logs them without re-raising. Callers (`send`, `recv` in the same file, and `CollectiveGroup._atomic_recv` / `_recv_tensor_list` in `collective_group.py`) don't check the return value, so on the receive side the caller's `torch.empty(...)` tensor is returned still holding uninitialized memory. Any subsequent operation on the channel is out of sync with the sender.
[body] - `ValueError: Unsupported object type: <random 32-bit integer>` (uninitialized bytes reinterpreted as an object-type enum), or
[body] - `_pickle.UnpicklingError: invalid load key, '\x00'.` (uninitialized bytes reinterpreted as a pickle stream).
[body] The exception is thrown in a worker thread (`_run_queue`), so the driver process stays alive and the job deadlocks silently until Gloo's per-pair TCP watchdog fires — 3 hours by default.
[body:code]     except Exception as error:
[body:code]         msg = (f"Broadcast failed on ProcessGroup {pg_name} rank "
